name: Shock Venus
idea: A heavy Venus sign whose cross has turned into a single lightning bolt: the bolt's horizontal jog is the Venus crossbar. You can draw it in two strokes, a circle and a zigzag.
rationale: CSP needs one symbol that works on a flag, a stencil, a wall and a ballot. A Venus everyone already reads, charged with a shock, says 'feminism with power' in one shape and points at the 'Shock' in the name. The monoline is built with care: one stroke weight matched to Archivo Black's stems, a point-symmetric bolt with parallel 33-degree legs, jog points flush with the ring's width, and a filleted junction so it reads as one stroke. In the primary lockup the bolt strikes down beside a red SHOCK, so the symbol and the name explain each other. The stacked alt is the justified poster block from the reference's protest-print world.
fonts: SpaceGrotesk-500 (corner captions in textured.svg only, outlined)
associationsChecked: BUF flash-and-circle and the Singapore PAP: the bolt hangs below the ring, attached at its base. It is never inside a circle and never crosses one. SS / sig runes: there is one bolt, never doubled. Its middle stroke is a horizontal jog (the crossbar), not the rune's steep diagonal. The shape has only 180-degree point symmetry, with no 4-fold rotation, so it cannot be turned into anything swastika-like. Poland's Strajk Kobiet: their mark is a filled, freestanding red bolt. Ours is a monoline bolt fused into a Venus ring, so the overlap is the idea, not the drawing. Rule: never use the bolt on its own. Indian election symbols (hand, lotus, broom, elephant, bicycle, hammer-sickle, etc.), the Labour rose and the US donkey/elephant: nothing alike. It is not the cliche of a Venus with a fist inside, and it is not pink. Also noted: at a glance it could read as a balloon on a zigzag string. Mild, and arguably a harmless 'party' pun. Not checked: an exhaustive trademark search. Venus-plus-bolt graphics exist in generic feminist merch, so a legal clearance search is still needed.
strengths: One idea, not two glued together: the bolt's jog does double duty as the Venus crossbar.
Two strokes by hand (a circle and a zigzag), so it can be stencilled, spray-painted or chalked, and drawn freehand at a rally.

Geometry is controlled: one stroke weight (44 units on a 200 ring), a 41-unit horizontal for optical balance, parallel 33-degree legs, jog points solved to sit flush with the ring (+1% overshoot), and a fillet on the concave junction.
The mark's stroke matches Archivo Black's stem at lockup size, so the symbol and wordmark read as one family. The ring sits against CULTURAL and the bolt strikes beside a red SHOCK.
Reads as a Venus at 16px. The zigzag is clear from 24-32px. The header lockup stays legible at 28px tall.
Holds up in one colour, in reverse on ink, and as a worn screenprint (textured.svg). It feels like protest print, not a corporate logo.
weaknesses: At 16px the bolt reduces to a kinked stem: it reads as 'Venus', but the electric idea only shows from about 24px up.
The red bolt sits in visual territory shared with Strajk Kobiet, and Venus-plus-bolt is not unheard of in feminist merch. Ownership depends on this exact geometry and on never showing the bolt alone.
The mark is tall and narrow (about 1.8:1), so square avatars and favicons leave empty side space. A dedicated app-icon tile (the mark on a red or ink square) would be stronger.
The red mark disappears on red grounds and is only medium contrast on ink (about 3.2:1). A paper or ink version is needed on red.
The wordmark is plain Archivo Black in caps: confident and credible, but not custom. In the two-line header lockup the caps are only about 10-11px tall at 28px, which is legible but tight.
In the stacked alt, PARTY is tracked about 0.085em wider than SHOCK to justify the block. A trained eye will see the rhythm change.
The junction is asymmetric by design: a crisp convex shoulder on the left, a fillet on the right. At poster scale some people may read that as a flaw.
The master marks are clean geometry. The handmade, dry-brush side of the reference only appears in the textured version.
